title: Physics I for the life sciences
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Apply kinematics, Newton's laws, energy and momentum, rotation and torque, biomechanics, fluids at rest and in flow, heat and thermodynamics, oscillations, waves and sound, with biomedical examples.

blocks.deliverable: Solve a two-body problem with free-body diagrams.
Apply conservation laws to a fall and a collision.
Compute the biceps force needed to hold a weight.
Week 7 midterm; apply continuity and Poiseuille's law to blood vessels.
Estimate heat lost by sweating during exercise.
Compute decibel levels and an ultrasound wavelength.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Biomechanics report: compute the forces in the elbow or lower back for a lifting task, and the change in blood flow when a vessel narrows, using Poiseuille's law.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
